paper_title: Towards a More Inclusive AI Progress and Perspectives in Large Language   Model Training for the Sámi Language
caption: The distribution of tokens and sentences across different domains in the SALT dataset is shown.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of sentences (in thousands, labeled as "Sentences (K)") across various content categories in the SALT dataset, as described in the paper "Towards a More Inclusive AI Progress and Perspectives in Large Language Model Training for the Sámi Language." The horizontal axis lists the categories in the following order: Administrative, Religion, Non-fiction, Fiction, Law, News, Science, and Blogs. The vertical axis represents the number of sentences, scaled linearly from 0 to 800 in increments of 200. Each category is represented by a single vertical bar colored in a uniform shade of red, with the exact number of sentences labeled in blue text above each bar. The values for each category are as follows: Administrative (525K), Religion (50K), Non-fiction (190K), Fiction (35K), Law (23K), News (902K), Science (110K), and Blogs (2K). The bars are arranged in the order of the categories along the x-axis, not sorted by value. The tallest bar corresponds to the News category (902K sentences), while the shortest corresponds to Blogs (2K sentences). There are no visual groupings, stacking, or additional annotations beyond the numerical labels.
